That's how outages get worse instead of better'; outlier detection fields consecutive5xxErrors, interval, baseEjectionTime ('Doubles on repeat offenses') and maxEjectionPercent ('never eject more than half the hosts'); a high limit 'can cause Istio to eject every backend pod, leaving you with zero capacity'. brief.situation: You run the service mesh for Fernvale Market, a fictional online grocer on Kubernetes with Istio. At 11:20 product pages are slow and ratings calls fail about a third of the time. One of the three ratings pods, ratings-v1-c, sits on node w3, which has a failing disk, and answers 503 after about 8 seconds. The weekly sale opens at 12:00 and triples traffic.
handover: A VirtualService for ratings was changed last month to 'make it more reliable'.
Node w3 is cordoned for disk replacement tomorrow; ratings-v1-c was scheduled there before the cordon.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the product page, the ratings pods and the mesh policy between them.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

virtualservice.networking.istio.io/ratings configured

then.log: More retries mean more load on the two pods that work.

writeup.question: For the record: what the mesh was doing, what you changed, and why those settings.

parts.label: What
parts.criteria: Ties the 503s to one pod and the slowness to the retry policy.
parts.modelAnswer: istio_requests_total put every 503 on ratings-v1-c; the VirtualService retried ten times at up to 30 s each with no timeout, tripling load on a and b.

parts.label: Changed
parts.criteria: Bounds retries with a per-try timeout inside an overall timeout, and ejects the bad pod with outlier detection.
parts.modelAnswer: timeout 3s with 2 retries at 1s per try on 5xx and connect failures; outlierDetection consecutive5xxErrors 3, interval 10s, baseEjectionTime 30s, maxEjectionPercent 50.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Explains why more retries, deleting the pod or ejecting everything would not help.
parts.modelAnswer: Retries multiply load; the replacement pod lands on w3 again; a 100% ejection limit can leave no pods at all under load. p99 back near 0.4 s before 12:00.

saleDown.headline: The retries took the healthy pods down
saleDown.body: Every call to the failing pod was retried up to ten times at 30 s each. Under sale traffic that load landed on the two pods that worked. Bound retries with a per-try timeout inside a route timeout.

ejectAll.headline: An ejection policy that can remove every pod
ejectAll.body: One 5xx and a 100% limit means a short blip during the sale can eject a and b too, leaving ratings with no endpoints for five minutes. Keep maxEjectionPercent below 100.

healthy.body: You read the policy and the per-pod metrics, bounded retries inside a timeout, let the mesh eject the failing pod with a safe limit, and checked p99 before the sale.

scoring.modelReasoning: The per-pod request metrics put every 503 on ratings-v1-c, the pod on the failing node, and show the other two pods carrying about three times their normal rate. The VirtualService retries 5xx ten times at up to 30 s per try with no route timeout, so each call that meets the bad pod turns into up to ten slow calls spread over the good ones. Bound it: a 3 s route timeout, 2 retries at 1 s per try. Then let the mesh stop sending to the bad pod: outlier detection with consecutive5xxErrors 3 and maxEjectionPercent 50, so it is ejected but the pool can never be emptied. Deleting the pod brings it back on the same node, restarting the gateway changes nothing because retries happen in productpage's sidecar, and more retries add load. Check p99 before the sale.
